t: Britain's last coal power station, Ratcliffe-on-Soar, shut on 30 September 2024. That ended 142 years of electricity made from coal.
Dinorwig, a power station hidden inside a Welsh mountain, can go from nothing to about 1,700 megawatts in around 16 seconds when it's on standby.
When England's 1990 World Cup semi-final shootout ended, Britain's demand for power jumped by 2,800 megawatts. It's the biggest TV surge on record, as the country got up and put the kettle on.
A 765 km power cable runs from Lincolnshire to Denmark. National Grid calls it the world's longest land and subsea electricity link.
Norwegian gas can reach the Yorkshire coast through a 1,166 km pipe under the North Sea. It was the world's longest subsea pipeline when it was built.
Godalming in Surrey is credited with the world's first public electricity supply, switched on in 1881. It was abandoned about three years later.
Scotland has a power station inside a mountain. Cruachan's machinery sits in a cavern about 400 metres below its reservoir, and the Queen opened it in 1965.
Europe's largest LNG terminal is on the Isle of Grain in Kent, where tankers bring chilled gas from across the world.
Hornsea 2, 89 km off the Yorkshire coast, has 165 turbines and can power about 1.4 million UK homes.
Britain's first full day without coal power since the Industrial Revolution was as recent as 21 April 2017.
